html:
The Yanomami are an Indigenous people of about 35,000 who live in some 200 to 250 villages in the Amazon forest on the border between Venezuela and Brazil.

A village usually lives in one large round communal house, the shabono, around an open plaza. They grow plantains and manioc in forest gardens and hunt, fish and gather, moving gardens every few years. Shamans use a snuff called yakoana to contact spirits.

They had little contact with outsiders until the mid 1900s. The American anthropologist Napoleon Chagnon made them famous with his 1968 book "The Fierce People", which many scholars and the Yanomami themselves rejected as distorted. In the late 1980s thousands of gold miners invaded their land in Brazil, bringing disease and violence; in 1993 miners killed Yanomami villagers at Haximu. Brazil set aside a large Yanomami territory in 1992, but illegal mining returned. Their spokesman Davi Kopenawa became known worldwide. Their neighbours include the Ye'kuana and the Hoti.
sum: The Yanomami are an Indigenous people of about 35,000 who live in some 200 to 250 villages in the Amazon forest on the border between Venezuela and Brazil.
